description: Agent Capacity: submit the scaling plan for when capacity runs out, with the load now: the plan with each trigger (what fires it, the metric, the threshold, the action and who acts), the lead time in days to add capacity once a trigger fires, the maximum scale with its unit, what happens when the maximum is reached (queue, shed, refuse, degrade, escalate or none) with who owns that step, and the plan as written, read for wording such as when needed, as demand grows or scale as required; and the current capacity, load and daily growth in load. The signed report gives every trigger with its threshold, action, owner and any wording that names no threshold, the runway before the load reaches the capacity at the current growth against the lead time with the margin, the maximum with the days until the load reaches it, and the step at the maximum with its owner, and counts them, and names an absent scaling plan: no trigger named, a lead time at or over the runway, no maximum scale and nothing stated for when the maximum is reached; then triggers with no threshold or with judgment wording, triggers with no owner, a step at the maximum with no owner, a runway under twice the lead time and a maximum the load reaches within 90 days, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No lead time, no current capacity, load or growth, or no plan text leaves the plan unverified. This reads the plan for adding capacity against the burn it must keep ahead of: where work goes when it hits a spending limit is wever_breach-path-check, whether alerts carry a threshold and an owner is wever_observability-alert-check and when a decision passes to a person is wever_escalation-threshold-check. Verdict capacity_scaling_absent, capacity_scaling_partial, capacity_scaling_unverified or capacity_scaling_ready. POST /api/capacity-scaling-check. Reads the load and capacity records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Capacity reads an agent’s own load and capacity records and checks the load against the capacity that exists: work in hand against the stated limit, a queue against its target wait, concurrent runs against the cap, an allowance’s burn against its period, a backlog across a window, spare capacity against the reserve, the scaling plan against the burn, and admission at capacity against written priority rules. Beside it, the Agent Limits checks such as wever_limit-substrate-check read whether a limit sits in code or in prose and how it is scoped, changed and seen, while a capacity check reads the load itself against the capacity; wever_commitment-deadline-check reads promised hours against due dates, while the workload check reads the work in hand against the stated limit over time; and the Agent Triage checks such as wever_triage-priority-check read how queue items are ranked, reviewed and closed, while the queue, backlog and throttle checks read waits, size and admission against capacity. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-capacity-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-capacity/.

burn_per_day.description: How fast load grows, per day.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

at_maximum.description: What happens when the maximum is reached.

lead_time_days.description: Days to add capacity once a trigger fires.

max_scale.description: The most capacity the plan can reach.

text.description: The plan as written, read for wording such as when needed or as demand grows.
